scenario: AITA for not wanting to be friends with my group anymore? | So I just finished my freshman year in college, and I found myself a pretty good friend group. I’ve always been really shy so the fact that I‘m part of a group means a lot to me. However, I’m the only one (in a group of 8) that is not in our school’s Honors College. Many people, including them, have assured me that this doesn’t mean they’re smarter than me or harder working than me, and I’ve accepted that. However, Honors College people all have some required courses to take that are just for them, so they all have classes together without me. And sometimes when we hang out, everyone talks about their classes and I feel completely left out. In addition, I found out that next year, they’re all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can’t live there since I’m not in Honors College and I already feel left out enough. Now that they’ll all live together, it’s even more likely they’ll end up hanging out without me just because they’re all living together and just happen to run into each other and how can I blame them for that?? I have tried to talk to a couple of them about it and one in particular said that I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy that they can live together but I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they’d realize that 7 people of an 8 person group living together is rather unfair. I don’t want to have to start over and find new friends but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. AITA?

But here's the thing: I'm the only one in a group of eight who isn't in our school's Honors College. When we hang out, everyone talks about their classes, and I feel completely left out. To make things worse, I found out that next year, they're all living in the Honors College dorm building together. Do I expect my friends to make an effort to include me even though they're living together and have different class schedules? Is that a fair expectation, or am I putting too much pressure on them? On the other hand, I should also reflect on whether I'm being too sensitive. Maybe my friends don't realize how their living situation and class schedules are affecting me. Communication is key here, but it seems like one of them at least doesn't want to engage in that conversation. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Could I find ways to stay connected with them despite the distance and different schedules? Maybe setting up regular hangouts or finding activities we can all participate in outside of school and dorm life. It's also important to consider my own well-being. If staying in this friendship group is causing me significant stress and unhappiness, maybe it's worth exploring other social circles. College is a time to meet new people and build different kinds of relationships, so I shouldn't feel like I'm stuck in one group. However, I don't want to give up on the friendships I've already built. It's challenging to balance the desire for inclusion with the reality of my friends' circumstances. If my friends are unwilling or unable to make an effort to include me, then it might be healthier for me to seek out new friendships where I feel more valued and included. But I also don't want to jump to that conclusion without giving it some serious thought and trying different approaches to improve the situation. So, to sum up, I need to: 1. Explore the possibility of finding new friends if the current situation doesn't improve. 5. Make a decision that prioritizes my well-being and happiness.
